subject: Pricing simulation request: marginal vs blended ladder for 12-month commit
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Liu <jason@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing simulation request: marginal vs blended ladder for 12-month commit

Hi Jason / EdgeHealth procurement team,

Thanks again for yesterday's call — appreciate the transparency on expected growth for Q3/Q4. To keep the momentum, can you share a simple 12-month usage forecast (monthly tokens by workload class) so we can run side-by-side simulations of two pricing approaches you asked about:

- Marginal per-token ladder (breakpoints with marginal pricing at each band)
- Blended effective rate (single blended rate after applying discounts)

Quick asks:
1) Can you upload a one-tab forecast (monthly tokens) — a single file is easiest.
2) Are there any constraints we should model (e.g., hard commit floors, rebate clawbacks, or usage smoothing expectations)?

We'll run three commit-tier scenarios (Conservative / Baseline / Aggressive) and return a short one-pager showing effective unit economics, estimated monthly invoice, and suggested breakpoint adjustments. Ben will own the simulation and Laura will coordinate terms.

If that sounds right, please send the forecast (or drop in the Drive link).

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jason Liu <jason@edgehealth.com>, procurement@edgehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-21T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing sims attached — marginal vs blended (initial pass)

Team / Jason,

I ran three commit scenarios using the attached forecast. Key items in the CSV: effective unit price under marginal ladder, blended effective rate, monthly invoice projection, and a sensitivity column showing the delta if the Sep spike is +/–20%.

Short summary:
- Marginal ladder gives EdgeHealth the most upside if growth happens (lower incremental token price above breakpoints).
- Blended rate simplifies invoicing and is attractive if you prefer predictability, but it raises the effective rate in the early months under the Baseline scenario by ~8–12%.
- For the Sep marketing uplift, marginal ladder reduces month-over-month cost by ~15% vs blended in the Aggressive scenario.

I've left three recommended breakpoint sets (Conservative / Baseline / Aggressive) in the sheet. Two practical negotiation points we should confirm: whether breakpoints are calendar-month based or trailing-30d, and whether we apply a quarterly true-up vs annual true-up.

Attachment: rdw_pricing_simulation_20270422.csv (simulation + notes)

If this aligns, Naomi / Laura — I suggest we propose a hybrid that uses a marginal ladder for incremental usage but guarantees a blended floor for the first quarter to limit invoice volatility for EdgeHealth. That gets both predictability and upside.

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Deals Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Jason Liu <jason@edgehealth.com>

Date: 2027-04-21T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sims attached — marginal vs blended (initial pass)

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A couple clarifying Qs:
1) In your hybrid proposal, how would credits/overage be calculated if we miss the Baseline for Q1 but hit it for Q2 — do we true-up quarterly or annually?
2) Any operational complexity on Redwood's side for trailing-30d breakpoints vs calendar-month? We have internal billing tied to calendar months and prefer not to have misaligned windows.

Also can you provide a one-page summary that we can share with our CFO and procurement team (short, one table + recommended breakpoints)?

If you can send that today, procurement will run an internal check and then we'll ask Legal to start a statement-of-work if numbers look good.

—Jason

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jason Liu <jason@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@edgehealth.com
Date: 2027-04-22T16:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing simulation request: marginal vs blended ladder for 12-month commit

Jason —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a one-pager that explains the hybrid approach, shows the three breakpoint options, and includes a worked example for Q1 true-up logic (quarterly true-up with annual settlement as default; we can switch to monthly if you need). Highlights:

- Proposed compromise: Baseline breakpoints at 5M / 20M / 60M tokens with marginal deltas of $0.0009 / $0.0006 / $0.00035; blended floor for first 90 days equal to the Baseline blended rate.
- True-up: quarterly true-up by default; annual settlement for billing reconciliation. We noted calendar-month windows are operationally easier for EdgeHealth — Redwood supports calendar-month breakpoints (we'll align billing windows in the SOW).
- Attachments: one-pager + proposed legal-ready terms. If that works, we'll route to Legal/Finance to draft a short SOW and an Appendix that codifies the breakpoint ladder and true-up cadence.

Attachments: rdw_pricing_onepager_edgehealth.pdf, proposed_pricing_terms_edgehealth.pdf

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement confirms baseline floor for Q1 by EOD tomorrow.
2) If confirmed, Legal will prepare SOW + Appendix; Finance will provision the commit account.
3) Pilot period: first 90 days blended floor, then ladder applies per calendar-month breakpoints with quarterly true-up.

Ben / Laura — please prepare the SOW template and draft the Appendix with the specific breakpoint math and invoice examples.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
